record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Show that the hypersurface X={x+x^2y+z^3+t^2=0} in C^4, which is known to be an exotic C^3, is not biholomorphic to C^3; more generally, prove the same for other known hypersurface examples in C^n that are exotic C^(n-1).

evidence.quote: 2.6. PROBLEM. Verify that the hypersurface X = {x + x2y + z3 + t2 = 0} ⊂ C4, which is known to be an exotic C3 (L. Makar-Limanov [ML; KML 2]), is not biholomorphic to C3. The same for other known hypersurfaces in Cn, which are exotic Cn− 1’s (see [Za 3]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let X ⊂ ℂ⁴ be the smooth affine complex hypersurface defined by
    X = { (x, y, z, t) ∈ ℂ⁴ : x + x²y + z³ + t² = 0 }.
It is known that X is diffeomorphic to ℝ⁶ and is not algebraically isomorphic to ℂ³ (it carries fewer algebraic 𝔾ₐ-actions than ℂ³; equivalently, its Makar–Limanov invariant is nontrivial), so X is an "exotic" affine 3-space.

Prove that X is not biholomorphic to ℂ³, i.e. that there is no biholomorphism between X (with its complex-analytic structure inherited from ℂ⁴) and the complex affine space ℂ³.

More generally, for the known families of smooth affine hypersurfaces Y ⊂ ℂⁿ that are diffeomorphic but not algebraically isomorphic to ℂⁿ⁻¹ (exotic ℂⁿ⁻¹'s), prove that no such Y is biholomorphic to ℂⁿ⁻¹.
artifact.status_search_result: The algebraic version of the problem was resolved by Makar-Limanov (1996), who showed that the Koras–Russell cubic threefold X = {x + x²y + z³ + t² = 0} is not algebraically isomorphic to ℂ³. The holomorphic (biholomorphic) version, however, remains an open problem: standard algebraic invariants such as the Makar-Limanov invariant are not holomorphic invariants, and recent work (e.g., A¹-contractibility results of Hoyois–Krishna–Østvær, 2014, and the trivial Makar-Limanov invariant of the cylinder X × ℂ shown by Dubouloz, 2009) underscores that the biholomorphic classification of these exotic affine threefolds is not settled.

status_evidence.title: Koras–Russell cubic threefold - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Smooth affine complex threefolds diffeomorphic to C^3 ... not algebraically isomorphic to affine three-space.
status_evidence.claim: Algebraic non-isomorphism with ℂ³ is established; biholomorphic question is more subtle.

status_evidence.title: The cylinder over the Koras–Russell cubic threefold has a trivial Makar-Limanov invariant
status_evidence.snippet: Cylinder X × A^1 has trivial Makar-Limanov invariant.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that algebraic invariants distinguishing X from ℂ³ become trivial after stabilization, complicating any extension to the holomorphic category.

status_evidence.title: A1-contractibility of Koras–Russell threefolds
status_evidence.claim: Suggests these threefolds are very close to ℂ³ in motivic/homotopic categories, but biholomorphic distinction remains open.
